title: Vendor risk scorecard and contract-split experiments for procurement self-serve flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise procurement and security teams expect a unified intake that ties vendor risk posture to contract terms and pricing. Today Redwood’s process is manual and blocks fast self-serve adoption for customers that are low-to-moderate risk but still ask for SOC2/insurance proof and contract modifications. Goal: enable a safe self-serve procurement funnel by (1) automating a vendor risk scorecard from questionnaire answers, (2) using that score to split contract templates and pricing obligations, and (3) surfacing a self-serve SOC2 + insurance upsell for eligible accounts. This ticket scopes experiments, legal alignment, and engineering work to validate a scoring model and contract-split rules that reduce time-to-sign for low-risk accounts while preserving guardrails for high-risk customers.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard implementation that maps questionnaire -> numeric risk band (low/med/high) in the procurement portal
Contract-split logic implemented: low-risk -> standard EULA with SOC2 bundle opt-in; med/high -> sales-assisted contract flow
A/B experiment running with 10% of new procurement flows and instrumentation to measure time-to-sign and conversion
Legal signoff on contract templates and auto-generated exhibits for SOC2/insurance
Dashboard showing per-band counts, time-to-sign, and revenue impact
success_metrics: Reduce time-to-sign for low-risk vendors from baseline by >= 40%
Increase self-serve procurement conversion from 12% -> 30% among eligible accounts
No >1 compliance incident due to automated acceptance in first 3 months
Clear attribution of incremental ARR for contract-split pricing tiers
proposed_experiments: Experiment A: Lightweight scorecard (10-question form) -> deterministic banding -> automatic EULA + SOC2 upsell modal
Experiment B: Enhanced scorecard with 3rd-party metadata (domain reputation + infra tags) -> if low, show discounted standard contract
Experiment C: Price split test where low-risk self-serve gets tiered pricing (base + SOC2 bundle) vs flat enterprise price requiring sales
Control: current manual intake routed to sales/legal
deliverables: Scorecard spec (questions, weights, band thresholds) in Confluence
Two contract template variants (self-serve + sales-assisted) with exhibits for SOC2 and insurance
Procurement portal UI flows and copy for upsell modals
Backend rule engine to produce contract routing and price results
Experiment instrumentation and dashboard (time-to-sign, conversion, ARR attribution)
timeline: Week 1 (2025-02-12 to 2025-02-18): Draft scorecard + kickoff with Legal and Security
Week 2: Design mockups for self-serve flow, draft contract templates for low/med/high
Week 3: Engineering implementation of scorecard endpoint and routing rules; start A/B wiring
Week 4: Internal QA, security review, and soft launch to 10% of procurement traffic
Week 6 (by 2025-03-28): Collect initial metrics, legal retrospective, and decide roll/rollback
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Scorecard misclassifies a high-risk customer as low -> Mitigation: conservative thresholds + manual review for flagged categories
Risk: Legal pushback on automated contract acceptance -> Mitigation: include clear acceptance language, audit trail, and human fallback
Risk: Customers confused by pricing splits -> Mitigation: clear copy, compare view, and sales-assist CTA
Risk: Instrumentation gaps hide issues -> Mitigation: require release gating until dashboard shows end-to-end signals
